decisions.evidence: Maker R1: “paste a web address; it's validated and added”; Maker R4: “US1 Save — validated address.”
decisions.note: The specified and implemented URL-saving behavior conforms. Specification and implementation-review stages.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents only an “auto-derived title” and title fallback; R2 says the server fetches the page `<title>`; R4 again reports “auto-title with fallback.” Client R1 approves as written and Client R4 accepts without identifying the missing description, favicon, or preview-image collection.
decisions.note: The comprehensive save design collects only the title rather than all required page metadata. Bare approvals do not surface this difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1: “Edit & delete… fix titles”; Maker R4: “inline title edit.” Client R1 approves and Client R4 says the app matches the approved behavior, without mentioning description editing or editing before save.
decisions.note: Only post-save title editing is presented; editable title/description both before and after saving are not provided.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents “fix titles”; Maker R4 reports only “inline title edit.” Client R1 approves as written and Client R4 accepts the implementation.
decisions.note: The presented edit scope omits URL, description, tags, and note editing.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1: “remove bookmarks with a confirmation step”; Maker R4: “delete behind a confirmation step.”
decisions.note: Bookmark deletion is recorded and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R2: an existing normalized URL “is warned, not stored twice”; Maker R4 reports “duplicate → 409.” Client R2 says the plan sounds good; Client R4 accepts without requesting guidance into editing the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: Duplicates are prevented, but the user is given a warning/error rather than being guided to edit the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents only “see all bookmarks (newest first),” while the same comprehensive specification collects only a title; Maker R4 reports a “newest-first list” and no description/favicon support. Clients R1 and R4 approve without raising list content.
decisions.note: The list cannot expose the required description and favicon because those fields are absent from the presented data behavior; the readability-first requirement is therefore only partially fulfilled.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1: “open a link in a new tab”; Maker R4: “open in new tab.”
decisions.note: Selecting/opening a bookmark navigates to its original URL, which is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 offers a choice: “is tagging in scope for the first build or should it be deferred?” Client R1 selects: “I’d like tagging kept in the first build.” Maker R4 confirms tag assignment and tag filtering.
decisions.note: The offered deferral alternative would omit reference-required tag assignment and filtering; the client selects the reference-conforming alternative at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 defines tagging as “label bookmarks and filter by tag”; R2 calls its complete tagging coverage “create, assign, filter”; R4 reports “assign tags, filter by tag, GET /api/tags.” Neither client response requests existing-tag autocomplete.
decisions.note: Autocomplete is absent from the comprehensively enumerated tagging behavior. Keeping tagging in scope does not express awareness of this missing subrequirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 and R4 describe only “keyword search”; the presented model/edit scope contains no description or note content to search. Client R1 approves and Client R4 accepts without specifying searchable fields.
decisions.note: The search design cannot provide full-text search across title, description, note, and URL.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 and R4 say “keyword search” but never state whether matching is case-insensitive. Client responses approve generally without addressing case sensitivity.
decisions.note: The record does not establish whether search case handling conforms; the decision remains evidentially unresolved.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents keyword search plus a separate “filter by tag”; R4 repeats keyword search and tag filtering, with no `#tag` query syntax. Clients approve without mentioning tag-search syntax.
decisions.note: The comprehensive search behavior separates tag filtering and omits `#tag` search syntax.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 specifies “search by keyword” in the complete baseline specification; Maker R4 reports the same implemented behavior. No AND/OR/NOT, grouping, or quoted-operator rules are presented. Clients R1 and R4 approve generally.
decisions.note: Boolean operators and parenthesized search groups are omitted from the presented search scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 and R4 enumerate only keyword search and do not present quoted exact-phrase matching. Client R1 approves the specification and Client R4 accepts the implementation without raising it.
decisions.note: Exact quoted-phrase search is missing from the comprehensive search design.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 declares a complete baseline with four journeys—save, browse/find, edit/delete, and tags—and no read-later behavior; Maker R4 says “All four user stories delivered.” Clients approve without requesting unread marking.
decisions.note: Marking a bookmark as read-later/unread is omitted from the proposed and completed functional scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1's complete journey list contains no unread perspective; Maker R4's complete delivery report contains only save, browse/find, edit/delete, and tags. Client R4 accepts this version.
decisions.note: A separate unread-bookmark view is omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 and R4 enumerate the full approved feature set without any read/unread transition. Client responses approve and accept without raising it.
decisions.note: Marking an unread bookmark as read is omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents the complete baseline journeys and only single-bookmark edit/delete and tag operations; Maker R4 reports the completed stories with no selection or bulk actions. Clients approve without requesting them.
decisions.note: Multi-selection and bulk tag/read/archive/delete actions are absent from the presented scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 and R4 give comprehensive feature summaries but present no whole-current-filter action. Client R1 approves and Client R4 accepts.
decisions.note: Applying bulk actions to all bookmarks matching the current filter is omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 explicitly sets “Default newest-first ordering, no custom sort.” Client R1 approves as written; Maker R4 again reports a “newest-first list,” and Client R4 accepts.
decisions.note: The list has a fixed order rather than user-selectable sort keys.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 limits editing to titles in its complete specification; Maker R4 reports only inline title editing and no note viewing/rendering. Clients approve without mentioning notes.
decisions.note: Markdown bookmark notes and rendered note viewing are omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1's complete specification and R4's completion report contain no local page snapshot or PDF-preservation behavior. Client R1 approves and Client R4 accepts.
decisions.note: Local HTML snapshots and the PDF-download edge case are omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 and R4 comprehensively enumerate the application behavior without Internet Archive snapshot creation. Clients approve without raising it.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot support is omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents deletion but no archive action in the complete baseline; Maker R4 reports deletion only. Client R1 approves and Client R4 accepts.
decisions.note: Reversible archiving that hides bookmarks from ordinary lists/search is omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 and R4 present only deletion, with no distinct archive lifecycle. Both client responses approve the behavior without raising that distinction.
decisions.note: Because archive is absent, the required reversible-archive versus permanent-delete distinction is absent.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1's four complete journeys and Maker R4's delivered-story list contain no archive list or archived perspective. Client R4 accepts the version.
decisions.note: A separate archived-bookmarks view is omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 presents keyword search and tag filters but no saved combination/bundle in the complete specification; Maker R4 reports the same feature families. Clients approve without requesting bundles.
decisions.note: Reusable bundles containing search terms and included/excluded tags are omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 explicitly states “No import/export from other browsers/services.” Client R1 says “Approve the specification as written” but does not state the import expectation or difference.
decisions.note: Netscape HTML import is explicitly excluded. General approval is not an accepted-divergence response.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 explicitly states “No import/export from other browsers/services.” Client R1 approves as written without independently identifying or accepting the missing export requirement.
decisions.note: Netscape HTML export is explicitly excluded; bare approval does not qualify as explicit acceptance of the divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker R1 specifies “Default newest-first ordering, no custom sort,” and presents no displayed-items or font-size settings; Maker R4 again reports fixed newest-first browsing. Clients R1 and R4 approve without discussing personal display settings.
decisions.note: Adjustable default sort and other display-related user settings are omitted.
